narrative:
The model predicts an 85% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and the fact that you have received other job offers. These stood out as the strongest drivers compared with employees the model predicted would stay.

Your 6–10 years of total experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many who are expected to stay have only 1–5 years, your longer background appears to signal greater mobility and outside options. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in this organization also contributed to the “will leave” direction; the model sees this mid-range tenure as a common point when people begin looking elsewhere. Finally, receiving other job opportunities strongly increased the likelihood of departure. Most employees predicted to stay never receive such offers, so this factor carried significant weight in your case.

The organization should review how it supports mid-tenure staff with external prospects, especially in the medical sector. You may want to reflect on whether improved recognition, better work-life balance, or clearer promotion paths could change your outlook before making any decisions.
